title: SII Vol. 18 No. 293 — Guttal
summary: Broken slab lying on the platform of a neem tree in front of the temple of Chenna Kesava (also called Surya-Narayana)

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 294 — Kengonda
summary: Slab set up near the temple of Kallesvara

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 295 — Haralahalli
summary: Slab set up against the front wall of the house of Honnappa Byadagi

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 296 — Haralahalli
summary: Slab set up against the front wall of the house of Honnappa Byadagai

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 298 — Guttal
summary: Hero-stone lying in front of the temple of Chennakesva

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 299 — Chaudadanpur
summary: This inscription is a composite record of two grants of land and refers to the rule of Ahavaditya Vikamaditya over Banavase-nadu

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 300 — Haralahalli
summary: Slab set up against the front wall of the house of Honnappa Byadagai

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 301 — Kanavalli
summary: Slab built into a wall inside the temple of Durga

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 302 — Honnatti
summary: This inscription refers to the rule of Maamandalesvara Joyideva and is dated in Plavamga Kartika Su

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 303 — Havanur
summary: This badly mutilated inscription refers to Vikramaditya and to a Yadava king

title: SII Vol. 18 No. 304 — Hulihalli
summary: This fragmentary and undated inscription refers to Joyideva and seems to record the death of a hero (name lost), probably the son of a certain Boviya-Nayaka, in a fight
